title: Joint Tail Limits for Extreme Quantile Treatment Effects on the Treated
banked_reason: D0.5.G delivered subfield below field floor; paper_score_ceiling 6.7 < 7.4; salvageable=false
gap_reasons: it does not establish optimal inference for the QTT estimand.
Generality is sharply limited by public alpha, the exactly known propensity and covariate density, and the exact multiplicative untreated-outcome model
the note gives componentwise fixed-law obstructions but leaves the complete attainable drift and inverse-law classification open
paper_score_ceiling 6.7 < 7.4, so the graded tier 'field' is capped at 'subfield'.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery derived the critical marked-Poisson law, a plug-in interval, and qualified high-count drift results; the final math review passed with no findings. The field-tier claim failed at D0.5 because the interval is procedure-specific and the rigid known-design model does not establish an estimand-level uncertainty frontier. A broader model, optimal inference or lower bounds, and a fuller nonlinear drift classification remain for a new specialization.
tldr: At the critical lower-quantile level \(\tau_n(t)=t n^{-\alpha/(\alpha+1)}\), the actual self-normalized inverse-weighted control quantile is governed by a weighted marked-Poisson inverse, while the treated empirical quantile has a deterministic first-order limit; empirical boundary marks therefore support a data-only Poisson-calibrated ninety-percent interval. Above the critical level, the weighted score is stable, and the linear QTT limit holds uniformly when \(R_{C,n}=\bar\tau_n^{1+\delta/\alpha}/b_n\) and \(R_{T,n}=\bar\tau_n^{1+\delta}/b_n\) vanish. A fixed treated flat-stretch law proves full-class worst-case sharpness of the treated condition; under strict mark-envelope slack \(c_g<1<C_g\), fixed compensated diagonal tubes prove worst-case sharpness of the control condition. If \(c_g=1\) or \(C_g=1\), normalization forces uniform marks and no control-side necessity claim is made. For polynomial levels the sufficient elbow is \(\zeta_T=\alpha/\{(\alpha+1)(1+\delta)\}\), which exceeds \(\zeta_C=\alpha^2/\{(\alpha+1)(\alpha+\delta)\}\).
gap: Avella-Medina, Davis, and Samorodnitsky impose their condition (25), a positive finite conditional-to-marginal lower-tail ratio near the propensity boundary, before obtaining their intermediate-quantile limit. In the present coupled model, the conditional lower tail is zero for \(x^\alpha>y\) and one for \(2x^\alpha\le y\), so that ratio cannot be uniform. Zhang's extreme-QTE Poisson theory instead assumes strict overlap.
fill: The project derives the joint finite-dimensional critical law, proves an empirical-mark plug-in theorem strong enough for uniform percentile calibration, constructs a capped data-only ninety-percent interval with length of order \(\tau_n\), and separates the high-count stable score from the additional local drift needed for linear quantile inversion.
